q: 1. The interest calculated on the basis of 365 days a year, is known as
explain: Exact simple interest uses the actual 365 days (366 in leap year) in a year for the time period, as opposed to ordinary simple interest which uses a 360-day year.

q: 2. If P is principal amount, i is the rate of interest per annum and n is the number of periods in years, the compound amount factor (CAF) is
explain: The compound amount factor converts a present sum to its future value: F = P(1+i)^n, so CAF = (1+i)^n.

q: 3. If F is the future capital accumulated in n years at the rate of interest i per annum, then present worth is
explain: Present worth is obtained by discounting the future sum back to the present: P = S/(1+i)^n, the inverse of the compounding relation.

q: 4. In a project equal investment is done for future value then it is called
explain: A sinking fund is a fund established by periodically setting aside money to pay off a debt or replace an asset in the future.

q: 5. The actual interest earned by a given principal is known as
explain: Effective interest is the real (actual) rate of return earned after accounting for compounding, as opposed to the nominal (stated) rate.

q: 6. In a cash-flow:
options: Time 0 is considered to be the present
A vertical arrow pointing up indicates a positive cash flow
An arrow pointing downward indicates a negative cash flow
explain: These are the standard conventions of a cash-flow diagram: the present is Time 0, upward arrows represent receipts (positive), and downward arrows represent disbursements (negative).

q: 7. If P = Rs. 1000, r=8%, Time = 5 yrs find the simple interest.
explain: Simple Interest = $(1000 \times 8 \times 5) / 100 = 400$.

q: 8. A person took a loan of Rs 100,000 for 10 years at 11% compound interest. The person desires to pay off the amount in 10 equal annual installments. The amount of installments is:
explain: Using the capital recovery factor A = P × [i(1+i)^n / ((1+i)^n − 1)] with P = 100,000, i = 0.11, n = 10 gives A ≈ Rs 5638.

q: 12. The sum of principal and compound interest is known as compound amount which is computed by the formula
explain: The standard compound interest formula for the total amount is $A = P(1+r)^n$.

q: 13. The relation between nominal interest rate and effective interest rate (i) is given by
explain: The effective rate accounts for compounding frequency (m) per year.

q: 14. If Interest rate is 1% per month then the effective interest rate is ......
explain: Effective annual rate = (1.01)^12 - 1 = 12.68%, which is more than the nominal 12% because of monthly compounding.

explain: P/A is the (series) present worth factor, converting a uniform annual payment to present value. Note: Q23 and Q24 are worded alike; the key gives a for Q23 and b for Q24.

q: 17. If P, F and A represents present value and annual payment and future value respectively, then the present worth factor is ......
explain: P/F is the single-payment present worth factor, converting a future sum to present value: P/F = 1/(1+i)^n.

q: 18. If P, F and A represents present value and annual payment and future value respectively, then the Compound amount factor is ......
explain: F/P is the single-payment compound amount factor and F/A is the series compound amount factor, so the key accepts both a and c.

q: 19. If the amount of principal is same then the value of compound interest for same time period is
explain: Compound interest accrues interest on accumulated interest as well as principal, so for the same principal and period it is always greater than simple interest (for n > 1).

q: 20. Discounting is the process of ......
options: determine the future value of a cash flow
finding the present value of a cash flow
find the series of equal periodic payment
explain: Discounting converts a future cash flow to its present value.

26. Compounding is the process of converting ......
explain: Compounding moves a present value forward to a future value using F = P(1+i)^n.

q: 27. Discounting is the process of converting ......
explain: Discounting brings a future value back to its present value using P = F/(1+i)^n.

q: 28. The present value of an amount is ............as compared to future value.
explain: Due to the time value of money and the positive interest rate, a sum of money today is worth less than that same nominal sum in the future.

q: 29. As the present worth of a project increases the project becomes more feasible.
explain: Present worth is a standard metric for determining the economic feasibility and profitability of an engineering project.

q: 30. For the selection of any project minimum future worth should be
explain: The Future Worth (FW) must be at least zero to ensure the project does not result in a net loss by the end of its life.

q: 31. If P is the principal amount, i is the ratio of interest and n is the number of periods in a year then the interest factor is ......
explain: For simple interest, amount = P(1 + ni), so the interest factor is 1 + ni.

q: 32. If P is principle amount, i is the interest rate per year, N is the number of periods in years, the interest amount is:
explain: The interest amount earned is the future value minus the original principal: Interest = P(1+i)^N − P.

q: 33. IF P is the principal amount, i is rate of interest and n is the number of periods in years, then the interest factor is:
explain: For simple interest, the interest factor (the multiplier applied to principal to get total interest) is ni.

q: 34. For the analysis of any project, net present worth may be
explain: Depending on the cash flow and discount rate, the resulting NPW/NPV calculation can be any real number.

q: 35. In a cash flow diagram ......
options: time 0 is considered to be present
time 1 is considered to be end of the past period 1
a vertical arrow pointing up indicates a positive each cash flow
explain: Time 0 is the present, time 1 marks the end of period 1, and an upward arrow is a positive cash flow, so all statements hold.

q: 36. In a cash flow series ......
options: uniform gradient signifies that and income or disbursement changed by the same amount in each interest period
either an increase or decrease in the amount of cash flow is called the gradient
the gradient in a cash flow may be positive or negative
explain: A gradient is a constant increase or decrease in cash flow per period, so all statements are correct.

q: 37. If a is the base amount expenditure is the increases in the operation cost each year over a period of n years. The total cost of maintenance is ......
explain: With a base amount a and a yearly increase b, the cost in year n is a + (n - 1)b (the base year has no increase yet).

q: 38. Discounting is the process of...........
options: determining the future value of a cash flow
finding the present value of cash flow
finding the series of equal periodic payments
explain: Discounting is the process of converting a future cash flow into its equivalent present value using an interest/discount rate.

q: 39. If 's' is the future capital accumulate in 'n' years at the rate of interest 'i' per annum, the present worth is:
explain: Present worth is obtained by discounting the future capital: P = s/(1+i)^n.

q: 40. Discounting is the process of ..........
options: determining the future value of a cash flow
finding the present value of a cash flow
finding the series of equal periodic payments
explain: Discounting is the mathematical process of determining the present value of a payment or a stream of payments that is to be received in the future.

q: 42. Pickup the correct statement from the following
options: the change in the amount of money over a given time period is called 'time value' of money
the manifestation of the time value of money is termed as interest
interest on borrowing = present amount owed - original loan
explain: All three statements correctly describe aspects of the time value of money concept and how interest manifests and is calculated.

q: 43. As the present worth of a project, which criteria is followed?
explain: Present worth is fundamentally an economic evaluation criterion used to judge project feasibility.

q: 44. The discount rate that makes the net present value equal to zero is known as :
explain: The IRR is mathematically the 'break-even' discount rate where PV of benefits equals PV of costs.

q: 45. The suspension of repayment of debt or interest for a specified period of time is called
explain: A moratorium is a legally authorized temporary suspension of debt or interest repayment for a specified period.

q: 46. The discount of one unit of principal for one unit of time.
explain: The rate discount is defined as the discount applicable to one unit of principal over one unit of time — essentially the periodic discount rate.

q: 47. The exact interest earned during entire year is called ......
explain: Effective interest is the actual interest earned over a full year after compounding.

q: 48. Time value of money refers to relationship between
explain: Time value of money links the amount, the interest rate and the time period.

q: 49. If the interest rate is 6% per year then monthly interest rate is ......
explain: Equivalent monthly rate = (1.06)^(1/12) - 1 = 0.487%, which is below 0.5%.

q: 50. The product of CAF (SP) and PWF (SP) is ......
explain: CAF(SP) = (1+i)^n and PWF(SP) = 1/(1+i)^n, so their product is 1.
